title: Zenith Systems - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Discovery with Zenith on Private VPC deployment options. Discussed AWS PrivateLink vs VPC peering, cross-region constraints, IP addressing, NAT/egress costs, SOC2/HIPAA needs, KMS integration, and proposed next steps: share network diagram, security pack, pricing, and schedule technical deep-dive/benchmarks.
questions: Can Redwood support inter-region private connectivity?
Do you offer PrivateLink / Private Service Connect endpoints?
What are required firewall rules and port ranges?
How does KMS/HSM integration work for keys?
next_steps: Lena to send security package and SOC2 artifacts (by 2026-04-02)
Marcus to schedule technical deep dive and benchmark window (by 2026-04-06)
Zenith to share network diagram and CIDR allocation (by 2026-04-05)
Lena to send initial pricing for Private deployment and Dedicated capacity options (by 2026-04-02)
action_items: Lena Ortiz (AE): email security docs + SOC2 + architecture notes - due 2026-04-02
Marcus Chen (SE): propose benchmark plan and test dataset + runbook - due 2026-04-06
Maya Singh (Infra): share VPC CIDRs, expected peering regions, and current NAT setup - due 2026-04-05
Oliver Grant (Security): list compliance controls required (HIPAA fields, audit retention) - due 2026-04-05
transcript:
[00:00] Lena (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. Marcus, SE, is with me too. How's it going?
[00:08] Raj (CTO): Hey Lena, hi Marcus. Good, thanks. Ready to dig in — Sofia and Maya are on for the infra specifics.
[00:14] Marcus (SE): Great. Quick agenda: we want to understand your network constraints, region preferences, compliance needs, and then go over our Private deployment options.
[00:22] Tom (PM): Sounds good. We want a single-tenant option if possible because of data residency.
[00:28] Maya (Infra): Quick context: Zenith is on AWS, primarily us-west-2 and eu-west-1. We have a mix of on-prem colo for legacy stuff and want to avoid public internet traffic for inference calls.
[00:38] Marcus (SE): Perfect. So Redwood Private can be deployed into a customer VPC in a couple of ways: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (we call it private endpoints), or a dedicated VPC we manage with a VPC peering connection. Each has tradeoffs.
[00:52] Raj: Can you expand on the inter-region story? We need nodes in both us-west-2 and eu-west-1 and ideally low latency between them.
[01:00] Marcus: Right. Native AWS VPC peering does not support transitive peering across regions unless you use inter-region VPC peering which is possible but there are latency and cost implications. Another pattern is to use PrivateLink/Private Endpoints per region and route traffic via your own transit gateway or AWS Transit Gateway for hub-and-spoke. That gives you more control and supports cross-account.
[01:20] Maya: Transit Gateway is our current hub. We prefer us to terminate peering at our TGW. Is Redwood ok with connecting to a TGW?
[01:26] Lena: Yes, we can peer into a customer TGW. For Private deployments we can create an endpoint service in your account and you create the interface endpoints, or we can peer our dedicated VPC into yours. We typically avoid asking customers to open broad ingress; we prefer narrow security groups.
[01:40] Sofia (DevOps): What IP ranges do you need? We can't overlap CIDRs with our internal networks.
[01:45] Marcus: We'll need a /20 or /22 depending on scale. Typical starter is /22 for a couple of GPU hosts. We'll confirm after we size your concurrency. Non-overlap is required.
[01:55] Oliver (Security): What about egress — will calls to external data stores or telemetry hit our NAT gateway? We want to control egress costs and logging.
[02:02] Marcus: Good question. If you host the model in your VPC and we run nodes there, egress is local. But if we fall back to a different region or Redwood-managed capacity, traffic egress could traverse peering and incur charges. We can pin region and provide routing policies to avoid cross-region fallback.
[02:18] Raj: We also need KMS integration for model keys — does Redwood support bringing your own KMS/HSM?
[02:25] Lena: Yes, BYOK is supported. For Private we integrate with customer KMS for data at rest and you can bring HSM via Cloud HSM for additional controls. We also provide audit logs and can forward them to your S3 or SIEM.
[02:36] Oliver: Audit retention? We have retention policies for 7 years for certain logs.
[02:40] Marcus: We support configurable retention; for Private we can send logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies. There may be storage cost, but compliance is doable.
[02:48] Tom: How do you handle auth — SSO, RBAC? We need SAML/OIDC and tight RBAC per team.
[02:54] Lena: We support SAML SSO with SCIM for provisioning and per-route RBAC. In Dedicated/Private you can enforce your own IdP and roles.
[03:03] Maya: Any network ports/ports ranges we need to open on the firewall?
[03:07] Marcus: Mostly TLS on 443 for API traffic. For internal control plane and heartbeats we use a few ephemeral ports — we'll list them in the network guide. If you use PrivateLink, interface endpoints use ENIs in your subnets.
[03:19] Raj: Can you do private endpoints via AWS PrivateLink in eu-west-1? We have some regulatory constraints in EU.
[03:25] Marcus: Yes, PrivateLink is region-scoped so you'd need endpoints per region. For EU residency we can pin model data to only eu-west-1 and ensure no cross-region replication.
[03:34] Lena: Quick note on performance: Dedicated/GPU-hosted in your VPC will give lowest latency. Hosted (Redwood-managed) is fastest to stand up but introduces egress to our network. We recommend Dedicated Reserved for production with predictable throughput.
[03:46] Maya: About fallbacks: we don't want traffic to go out to a public cloud fallback if capacity is full. Is that something you can lock down?
[03:53] Marcus: Yes, we have routing policies — canaries and fallback are configurable. For strict isolation you can choose no-fallback and capacity-based throttling or dedicated capacity with overprovision.
[04:02] Sofia: Are there limits on VPC peering across accounts for you? We run many accounts.
[04:06] Marcus: We can operate in cross-account mode. If you want Redwood to host a dedicated VPC we peer into each account. You can also create interface endpoints per account and attach to our endpoint service — both are common patterns.
[04:18] Raj: Any minimum commitment for a Private deployment?
[04:21] Lena: There's typically a deployment/setup fee and a reserved capacity minimum for Dedicated. Pricing depends on GPU size and uptime SLA. I'll send a pricing grid after this call.
[04:30] Tom: For our pilot we want 100 qps bursty workload with mostly short contexts (<=256 tokens). Do you have recommendations on model and quantization?
[04:37] Marcus: For short contexts you can go with quantized LLMs and smaller variants to cut cost. Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and cache settings. For 100 qps you likely need multiple GPU hosts; we'll propose a sizing based on target P95 latency.
[04:48] Raj: Latency SLOs — can you hit 100ms P95 for generation?
[04:52] Marcus: Depends on model. For small quantized models yes; for larger ones P95 might be 200–1400ms depending on tokens. We'll run benchmarks in your VPC to get real numbers.
[05:02] Oliver: Security: SOC2, ISO, and HIPAA are relevant. Do you have artifacts we can share with our compliance team?
[05:08] Lena: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 certs and a HIPAA addendum. I'll drop the pack. We also provide penetration test reports upon NDA.
[05:16] Sofia: Network diagram — what do you need from us to set up endpoints?
[05:20] Marcus: CIDR blocks, subnets for endpoints, security group egress rules, route table attachments, and whether you use TGW. Also TLS cert requirements if you front with an internal ALB.
[05:29] Maya: One more thing: can your service work with our Private Service Connect on GCP? We have a mixed cloud footprint.
[05:35] Marcus: We support equivalent patterns: Private Service Connect for GCP, PrivateLink for AWS, and Private Endpoint constructs on Azure. Each is region-scoped and requires one endpoint per region. We can document the exact steps.
[05:45] Lena: Ok let's do next steps, quick recap. We'll send the security pack and SOC2 artifacts, Marcus will follow up with a technical deck and benchmark plan, and you share the network diagram and CIDRs.
[05:55] Raj: Great thanks everyone.
[05:57] Lena: Thanks all.
notes: Customer uses us-west-2 + eu-west-1; requires EU data residency for some workloads
Preferred network pattern: Transit Gateway hub-and-spoke with PrivateLink endpoints per region
Pilot sizing: 100 qps, short contexts <=256 tokens, recommend quantized small models + benchmarking in-customer VPC
